summary: Invoice.tax_cents taxes the gross subtotal, so discounted invoices are over-charged tax. Tax Decimal(self.taxable_cents()) (subtotal minus discount) instead, still rounded half-even with billing.money.round_cents, and add a test for a discounted, taxed invoice. One line in src/billing/invoice.py plus a test.

steps.title: Compute tax_cents on taxable_cents() instead of subtotal_cents()
steps.rationale: taxable_cents() already subtracts the discount; round_cents keeps half-even rounding and no floats.

steps.title: Add a test for a discounted, taxed invoice
steps.rationale: The issue's example: EUR 100.00, 10 % discount, 20 % tax -> tax 1800, total 10800.

steps.title: Run uv run pytest -q and uv run ruff check .

acceptance_criteria.text: A EUR 100.00 invoice with a 10 % discount and 20 % tax has tax 1800 and total 10800.
An invoice without a discount keeps its totals.
uv run pytest -q and uv run ruff check . pass.

risks: Rounding order: the discount is rounded before tax is applied, as the issue's example expects.
